text:
lina: hey team :wave: quick Q — golang SDK streaming users are seeing `unexpected EOF` / partial-JSON errors when our eventstream chunks split objects across frames. also some clients block under load (backpressure). anyone handled mid-stream auth refresh + retries cleanly?

jamal: a few patterns that worked for us: 1) treat each SSE `data:` payload as a fragment and reassemble by buffering until you detect a complete JSON object (balanced braces or newline-delimited), 2) add sequence IDs on server-side so client can reorder/dedup on reconnect.

sam: reassembly tip: use a small ring buffer + attempt incremental json.Decode on the buffered bytes. in go the `json.Decoder` can be used with `Decode` repeatedly but it needs full objects. we ended up accumulating bytes and trying `json.Valid(buf)` to check before decode. cheap and effective.

lina: example of how you did the incremental check? worried about memory under a noisy stream.

sam: sure — sketch: ```go
// pseudo
var buf []byte
for chunk := range incomingChunks {
  buf = append(buf, chunk...)
  for json.Valid(buf) {
    var obj map["string"]any
    dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(buf))
    if err := dec.Decode(&obj); err != nil { break }
    handle(obj)
    // remove consumed bytes -> use dec.InputOffset() to slice
    off := dec.InputOffset()
    buf = buf[off:]
  }
  if len(buf) > maxBuf { trimOrFail() }
}
```

jamal: +1 to that. also consider limiting goroutine concurrency for processing and using a bounded channel as backpressure. when the processing channel is full, you can pause reading from the HTTP body (or return early to let server retry).

olivia: on auth: tokens can expire mid-stream. our approach: upstream emits `retryable: true` and a monotonic `seq` with every message. Client treats auth-fail as reconnect case: refresh token, reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` header = last-seen-seq. server will resend or resume from next sequence. avoids trying to mutate headers mid-body.

lina: that matches our thinking — reconnect vs mutating headers. is there a graceful way to force a reconnect from server side so clients know to re-auth? status code? special event?

jamal: we send a short control SSE event: `event: control\ndata: {"type":"reauth","reason":"token_expired"}` then close connection with 401/440. client sees control event and does refresh+reconnect. less surprising than abrupt close.

sam: on the go client side: use a single reader goroutine that writes incoming raw chunks into a buffered channel of capacity N. processor pool consumes. if channel is full, block reader which naturally produces backpressure to TCP. avoid spinning new goroutines per chunk.

lina: good call. any gotchas with `io.Copy` vs manual Read?

jamal: io.Copy can hide chunk boundaries; manual Read into a fixed-size buffer gives you chunk slices you can append. but either is fine if you reframe as "stream of bytes" and handle incremental parsing. be careful with `bufio.Reader.ReadBytes('\n')` if server splits JSON across lines unpredictably.

olivia: we also included these small things: 1) server-side max-fragment-size header so clients can size buffers, 2) backoff jitter on reconnects, 3) idempotent event handlers.

lina: awesome — i'll prototype ring-buffer + seq-based resume. one last thing: retries on transient network errors — should client attempt resume automatically or surface to app?

sam: auto-retry up to a small retry budget, then bubble up. include metrics: resume_attempts, full_reconnects, last_seq_lost. helps ops tune.

ci-bot: deploy-check: devex/go-stream-parser v0.3.1 tests passed on linux-amd64, flakiness rate 0.9% -> keep an eye on integration SSE harness. :eyes:

lina: thanks all — i'll post a short RFC in #eng-runtime once i have the prototype and perf numbers. :thumbsup:
